Blocking demo (alert if not blocked)

The external script below has no license declaration at all, so it's classified Missing — a category that isn't in the default allowed list (publicDomain, permissive, weaklyProtective), making it a blocking candidate. It just calls alert(...), so you can see with your own eyes whether it ran.

Blocking only ever applies to external scripts — inline <script> content is classified for reporting but never blocked, since by the time it's observed it has typically already run (see the README's "How blocking works"). That's why this fixture uses an external .js file instead of an inline script.

  1. Turn on "Block non-allowed scripts on this device" in the popup (or "Enable blocking" in Options).
  2. Reload this page.
  3. Chrome: blocking is best-effort via declarativeNetRequest, which can only block a URL after it's been classified once — so the alert will still fire on this first reload. Reload again; now that the script's URL is cached as "missing", the block rule is in place and the alert should not fire.
  4. Firefox: if you've granted the optional "block scripts before they run" permission (Options prompts for it when you enable blocking), this is true first-load blocking — the alert should not fire even on the very first reload after enabling.
  5. Turn blocking back off and reload once more to confirm the alert fires again.

If you see the alert when you expected it to be blocked, check Options → "Clear cached classifications" (a stale cache entry from before you enabled blocking can otherwise persist) and reload again.
